name: Brigham Young University
header:
Brigham Young University
United States · Mathematics PhD; MS alternative
Ranking entry: 93. 2026 secondary rank93; ranking basis separate from official admissions evidence.
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• Endorsement and Honor Code agreement are application prerequisites for all applicants.
• Do not treat old GRE or TOEFL thresholds in the handbook as current requirements.
• The advertised annual stipend does not establish guaranteed summer support.

sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
A mathematics or related technical bachelor’s is sufficient: a year of proof-based advanced calculus and
another year of advanced proof-based mathematics are expected. University minimum GPA3.0; degree must
be completed before entry. UChicago satisfies the degree type, subject to individual preparation. International
applicants are permitted. Every applicant must meet the Honor Code and endorsement requirements. [s1] [s3]
[s7] [s8]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Create/verify a BYU NetID early: processing may take up to48 hours. Arrange ecclesiastical endorsement,
including a University Chaplain interview if not a member of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.
Agree to university standards; prepare references, records and any required English report. Do not assume a
secular-university application workflow. [s1] [s4] [s7]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No advance supervisor agreement is listed. Target the faculty below; confirm doctoral supervision and fall
2027 availability. Kyle Pratt explicitly welcomes contact about research projects, but this is not a guarantee of
a PhD place. Department: office@mathematics.byu.edu. [s1] [s11] [s34]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Use the application link provided by Mathematics and the existing NetID if you have one. Its public destination
is a university CMS preview page; the international-instructions page returned an access error, so the current
policy handbook supplies international rules. The application itself was not submitted or authenticated. [s1] [s3]
[s4]
Cycle verification [Standing rule]
The live departmental deadline and stipend are standing/undated, not an explicit fall 2027 announcement.
Current 2026-27 catalog exists; the accessible detailed PhD catalog record is 2024 and is labeled accordingly.
[s1] [s2] [s8] [s9]

sections.title: Deadlines by stage
sections.text:
Academic application [Conflict]
January 15 for spring/summer/fall entry, standing rather than explicitly 2027. Winter August 15 is exceptional
and often unfunded. The linked central workflow says12:00 a.m. Eastern (10 p.m. Mountain) on the listed date;
this is ambiguous about which midnight and is not 11:59 p.m. that evening. Submit a day early and confirm.
Department permits late consideration, while central instructions say forms close at deadline. [s1] [s4]

Funding consideration [Standing rule]
January 15 is the departmental full-consideration aid target. No separately dated 2027 fellowship competition
for an incoming mathematics student was established. Winter applicants often have no aid. [s1] [s5]
Reference receipt [Unresolved]
No independently published reference grace date was found. Central application status can show missing
references after submission, but admission cannot proceed until they arrive. Plan receipt by the January 15
target and confirm the midnight interpretation. [s1] [s4]
Test-score receipt [Unresolved]
No separate mathematics score deadline is published. Exempt applicants need no English test; otherwise
official agency reports are required. GRE is not required. [s1] [s3]
Supporting documents [Standing rule]
Initial unofficial PDF records and endorsement belong in the complete application. Final official transcripts
showing the conferred degree are required before the first semester/registration; the handbook also states
consequences if they remain missing at term end, which should not be treated as permission to delay. [s3] [s4]
Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
No mathematics fall 2027 acceptance deadline was verified. Follow the admission and funding offers, and
verify current April 15-resolution coverage separately. [s1] [s2]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Conflict]
Nonexempt applicants: IELTS7.0, each>=6; DET130, each>=125; Cambridge180/C; TOEFL old85 with
speaking22 and other sections21, or new-scale overall4.5 with each>=4 for tests from January 21, 2026.
Official reports only. Older departmental TOEFL580/600 statements are obsolete-scale text. [s3] [s5]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
A residential bachelor’s or higher from a listed country, including the United States, completed within24
months before intended entry qualifies. A recently completed UChicago degree therefore fits. Whether an
anticipated degree is enough at application is not explicit; request confirmation. Another exception requires
departmental petition and evidence, not a self-declared waiver. [s3]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Not required under the current mathematics checklist. It does not say whether an optional score would be
considered; do not relabel this as “not considered.” [s1]
GRE Mathematics [Conflict]
Not required under the current checklist. Older admission/handbook material gives a600 benchmark; that
conflicts with the current explicit rule and should not control. Optional-score treatment remains unverified. [s1]
[s6]

degrees” is narrower. Final official records with conferral follow admission. A UChicago-only US degree does
not trigger a foreign-degree evaluation merely because the applicant is international. [s1] [s3]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three letters; at least two should assess mathematical background and graduate-level potential. [s1]
Scholarship references [Unresolved]
No separate departmental first-year scholarship reference is published. External fellowship rules differ; the
three prominently linked US federal fellowships have citizenship restrictions and are not automatically
available to an F-1 applicant. [s1] [s2]
What sends the invitation [Unresolved]
Not established for the graduate mathematics portal. Public instructions from other BYU programs or
undergraduate applications were not assumed to apply. Confirm whether saving a referee sends the request or
a separate send action is required. [s4]
Before versus after submission [Unresolved]
The public graduate instructions show outstanding recommendations in the submitted application’s status
page. They do not establish whether invitations require submission or can be sent beforehand. [s4]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
The central status page marks missing materials, including recommendations and endorsement, with a red X
and provides follow-up links. A cleared requirement is the documented receipt check. [s4]
Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
Separate statements and recommendation sets are required for separate graduate programs. Replacement of
a received letter and cross-cycle reuse are not established; undergraduate reuse rules are not evidence for this
application. [s3] [s4]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Conflict]
The undated department page says aid is generally offered to admitted students: full tuition plus roughly
USD22,500/year for PhD or USD20,100/year for MS. It does not identify paid months, a 2027-28 rate,
fee/insurance coverage or guaranteed summer. Older handbook splits PhD support into15,000 fall/winter
plus7,500 spring/summer with limited summer funds; do not treat the total as an unconditional guarantee. [s2]
[s5]

Years of support [Unresolved]
No current guaranteed number of funded years was established. The handbook describes a four-year doctoral
plan after a master’s, but that is not a funding guarantee or a prohibition on bachelor’s-entry applicants. [s5]
[s8]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
No citizenship exclusion appears in the general departmental tuition/TA/RA offer description. Confirm individual
offer eligibility, work authorization and any teaching-language requirement; a listed external award may
impose separate restrictions. [s1] [s2]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Part-time TA or RA duties accompany ordinary support; the handbook describes20 hours/week and satisfactory
progress. It links continued PhD funding to timely qualifying examinations, including passing two of three by
the end of year2. Verify the current offer’s conditions. [s2] [s5]
Extra funding application [Unresolved]
No separate assistantship application appears in the public checklist; complete the degree application by the
funding target and inspect the form for a funding question. Competitive external fellowships require their own
applications. [s1] [s2]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
The department links NSF GRFP, NDSEG and DOE CSGF as larger competitive fellowships. These are not
generic international-student funding routes; verify the citizenship/residency rules in the shared funding notes.
Research/travel assistance is also described in the handbook, subject to progress and adviser support. [s2] [s5]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD50 per graduate program application. [s1] [s3]
Fee waiver [Conflict]
Mathematics expressly says it cannot waive application fees. Central policy permits a department to pay
exceptional applicants’ fees using OGS Form1, but this is not a published mathematics waiver scheme or a
promise of eligibility. [s1] [s3]

sections.title: Potential advisers and recent research
sections.text:
Algebraic / arithmetic geometry
Nathan Priddis
Mirror symmetry, Landau-Ginzburg models and K3 surfaces. [s12] [s13]
Associate Professor; availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2024 · Mirror Map for Landau-Ginzburg models with nonabelian groups

Tyler Jarvis
Numerical algebraic geometry and polynomial/analytic root finding; current laboratory also emphasizes
machine learning. Historical FJRW work should not alone be used to infer current PhD topics. [s14] [s15]
Professor and ACME director; topic and availability need confirmation.
Research evidence: 2025 · Generalized Aliasing Explains Double Descent and Informs Model Design
Recent paper demonstrates the current applied direction; algebraic geometry fit is adjacent.
Complex geometry
Jennifer Brooks
Several complex variables, CR geometry, Hermitian sums of squares, and harmonic mappings. [s16] [s17]
Professor; availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2026 · Applying the argument principle to count zeros of harmonic functions with poles
Number theory
Darrin Doud
Hecke actions on arithmetic-group homology and Galois representations; computational arithmetic. [s18] [s19]
Professor; availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2026 · Sums of two irreducible Galois representations and the homology of GL_n(Z)
Paul Jenkins
Modular/Maass forms, coefficient behavior, partitions and duality. [s20] [s21]
Professor and Associate Dean; availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2026 · Modular forms with only nonnegative coefficients
Nickolas Andersen
Modular and automorphic forms, half-integral weight and arithmetic congruences. [s22] [s23]
Associate Professor; availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2025 · Congruences like Atkin’s for generalized Frobenius partitions
Kyle Pratt
Analytic number theory, primes, sieve methods, L-functions and Diophantine problems. [s24] [s25] [s34]
Assistant Professor; welcomes research-project inquiries.
Research evidence: 2026 · On Page’s theorem and zero-free regions for Dirichlet L-functions
David Cardon
Analytic number theory and entire functions; recent work also treats Euclidean algorithms in quadratic rings.
[s28] [s29]
Professor; availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: October 2026 preprint · The exact Euclidean window of Z[sqrt(14)]
Jasbir Chahal
Elliptic curves, congruent numbers and Diophantine equations. [s30] [s31]
Professor with Fall 2026 teaching on current page; not labeled emeritus there.
Research evidence: 2024 · Some remarks on rational right triangles

Xian Jin Li
Zeta functions, explicit formulas and spectral/operator approaches to analytic number theory. [s32] [s33]
Professor; availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2023 · A Hilbert-Schmidt integral operator and the Weil distribution
Newest peer-reviewed item established from the official CV; do not interpret later preprint claims as established theorems.
Representation theory
Pace Nielsen
Ring and module theory, cancellation and infinite summation; representation-adjacent algebra rather than a
Lie-representation specialty. [s26] [s27]
Professor and Associate Chair; availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2026 · Algebraization of infinite summation

text:
Brigham Young University
United States · Mathematics PhD; MS alternative
Ranking entry: 93. 2026 secondary rank93; ranking basis separate from official admissions evidence.
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• Endorsement and Honor Code agreement are application prerequisites for all applicants.
• Do not treat old GRE or TOEFL thresholds in the handbook as current requirements.
• The advertised annual stipend does not establish guaranteed summer support.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
A mathematics or related technical bachelor’s is sufficient: a year of proof-based advanced calculus and
another year of advanced proof-based mathematics are expected. University minimum GPA3.0; degree must
be completed before entry. UChicago satisfies the degree type, subject to individual preparation. International
applicants are permitted. Every applicant must meet the Honor Code and endorsement requirements. [s1] [s3]
[s7] [s8]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Create/verify a BYU NetID early: processing may take up to48 hours. Arrange ecclesiastical endorsement,
including a University Chaplain interview if not a member of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.
Agree to university standards; prepare references, records and any required English report. Do not assume a
secular-university application workflow. [s1] [s4] [s7]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No advance supervisor agreement is listed. Target the faculty below; confirm doctoral supervision and fall
2027 availability. Kyle Pratt explicitly welcomes contact about research projects, but this is not a guarantee of
a PhD place. Department: office@mathematics.byu.edu. [s1] [s11] [s34]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Use the application link provided by Mathematics and the existing NetID if you have one. Its public destination
is a university CMS preview page; the international-instructions page returned an access error, so the current
policy handbook supplies international rules. The application itself was not submitted or authenticated. [s1] [s3]
[s4]
Cycle verification [Standing rule]
The live departmental deadline and stipend are standing/undated, not an explicit fall 2027 announcement.
Current 2026-27 catalog exists; the accessible detailed PhD catalog record is 2024 and is labeled accordingly.
[s1] [s2] [s8] [s9]
Deadlines by stage
Academic application [Conflict]
January 15 for spring/summer/fall entry, standing rather than explicitly 2027. Winter August 15 is exceptional
and often unfunded. The linked central workflow says12:00 a.m. Eastern (10 p.m. Mountain) on the listed date;
this is ambiguous about which midnight and is not 11:59 p.m. that evening. Submit a day early and confirm.
Department permits late consideration, while central instructions say forms close at deadline. [s1] [s4]

Funding consideration [Standing rule]
January 15 is the departmental full-consideration aid target. No separately dated 2027 fellowship competition
for an incoming mathematics student was established. Winter applicants often have no aid. [s1] [s5]
Reference receipt [Unresolved]
No independently published reference grace date was found. Central application status can show missing
references after submission, but admission cannot proceed until they arrive. Plan receipt by the January 15
target and confirm the midnight interpretation. [s1] [s4]
Test-score receipt [Unresolved]
No separate mathematics score deadline is published. Exempt applicants need no English test; otherwise
official agency reports are required. GRE is not required. [s1] [s3]
Supporting documents [Standing rule]
Initial unofficial PDF records and endorsement belong in the complete application. Final official transcripts
showing the conferred degree are required before the first semester/registration; the handbook also states
consequences if they remain missing at term end, which should not be treated as permission to delay. [s3] [s4]
Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
No mathematics fall 2027 acceptance deadline was verified. Follow the admission and funding offers, and
verify current April 15-resolution coverage separately. [s1] [s2]
English and GRE
English requirement [Conflict]
Nonexempt applicants: IELTS7.0, each>=6; DET130, each>=125; Cambridge180/C; TOEFL old85 with
speaking22 and other sections21, or new-scale overall4.5 with each>=4 for tests from January 21, 2026.
Official reports only. Older departmental TOEFL580/600 statements are obsolete-scale text. [s3] [s5]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
A residential bachelor’s or higher from a listed country, including the United States, completed within24
months before intended entry qualifies. A recently completed UChicago degree therefore fits. Whether an
anticipated degree is enough at application is not explicit; request confirmation. Another exception requires
departmental petition and evidence, not a self-declared waiver. [s3]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Not required under the current mathematics checklist. It does not say whether an optional score would be
considered; do not relabel this as “not considered.” [s1]
GRE Mathematics [Conflict]
Not required under the current checklist. Older admission/handbook material gives a600 benchmark; that
conflicts with the current explicit rule and should not control. Optional-score treatment remains unverified. [s1]
[s6]
Academic records
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Central policy requires unofficial PDF transcripts from every school attended; the mathematics shorthand “past
degrees” is narrower. Final official records with conferral follow admission. A UChicago-only US degree does
not trigger a foreign-degree evaluation merely because the applicant is international. [s1] [s3]
Mathematics-course list; Course descriptions [Unresolved]
No separate mathematics-course list or course-description attachment is published. Whether the current form
requests one, with its limit/format and upload method, remains unverified. [s1] [s4]

Recommendation letters
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three letters; at least two should assess mathematical background and graduate-level potential. [s1]
Scholarship references [Unresolved]
No separate departmental first-year scholarship reference is published. External fellowship rules differ; the
three prominently linked US federal fellowships have citizenship restrictions and are not automatically
available to an F-1 applicant. [s1] [s2]
What sends the invitation [Unresolved]
Not established for the graduate mathematics portal. Public instructions from other BYU programs or
undergraduate applications were not assumed to apply. Confirm whether saving a referee sends the request or
a separate send action is required. [s4]
Before versus after submission [Unresolved]
The public graduate instructions show outstanding recommendations in the submitted application’s status
page. They do not establish whether invitations require submission or can be sent beforehand. [s4]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
The central status page marks missing materials, including recommendations and endorsement, with a red X
and provides follow-up links. A cleared requirement is the documented receipt check. [s4]
Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
Separate statements and recommendation sets are required for separate graduate programs. Replacement of
a received letter and cross-cycle reuse are not established; undergraduate reuse rules are not evidence for this
application. [s3] [s4]
Written materials
Academic CV / resume; Personal / background statement; Research-interest statement; Research
proposal; Writing sample / thesis / research summary; Publications list; Scholarship essays; Other
short answers / materials [Unresolved]
Not separately specified in the current public mathematics checklist. Required/optional status, prompt, length,
formatting, and permission to upload papers or provide links remain unverified in the authenticated form. The
ecclesiastical endorsement is a separate required process, not a substitute essay. [s1] [s4]
Statement of purpose [Unresolved]
A statement of intent/purpose is described in graduate policy and the older handbook. Current
mathematics-specific prompt, length, formatting and text-box/upload method are not public. Earlier guidance
asks about educational/career objectives and how graduate study serves them (paraphrase); verify before
drafting to that old prompt. [s3] [s5] [s10]
Course-list document [Unresolved]
No separate mathematics-course list or course-description attachment is published. Whether the current form
requests one, with its limit/format and upload method, remains unverified. [s1] [s4]
Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [Conflict]
The undated department page says aid is generally offered to admitted students: full tuition plus roughly
USD22,500/year for PhD or USD20,100/year for MS. It does not identify paid months, a 2027-28 rate,
fee/insurance coverage or guaranteed summer. Older handbook splits PhD support into15,000 fall/winter
plus7,500 spring/summer with limited summer funds; do not treat the total as an unconditional guarantee. [s2]
[s5]

Years of support [Unresolved]
No current guaranteed number of funded years was established. The handbook describes a four-year doctoral
plan after a master’s, but that is not a funding guarantee or a prohibition on bachelor’s-entry applicants. [s5]
[s8]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
No citizenship exclusion appears in the general departmental tuition/TA/RA offer description. Confirm individual
offer eligibility, work authorization and any teaching-language requirement; a listed external award may
impose separate restrictions. [s1] [s2]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Part-time TA or RA duties accompany ordinary support; the handbook describes20 hours/week and satisfactory
progress. It links continued PhD funding to timely qualifying examinations, including passing two of three by
the end of year2. Verify the current offer’s conditions. [s2] [s5]
Extra funding application [Unresolved]
No separate assistantship application appears in the public checklist; complete the degree application by the
funding target and inspect the form for a funding question. Competitive external fellowships require their own
applications. [s1] [s2]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
The department links NSF GRFP, NDSEG and DOE CSGF as larger competitive fellowships. These are not
generic international-student funding routes; verify the citizenship/residency rules in the shared funding notes.
Research/travel assistance is also described in the handbook, subject to progress and adviser support. [s2] [s5]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD50 per graduate program application. [s1] [s3]
Fee waiver [Conflict]
Mathematics expressly says it cannot waive application fees. Central policy permits a department to pay
exceptional applicants’ fees using OGS Form1, but this is not a published mathematics waiver scheme or a
promise of eligibility. [s1] [s3]
Conflicts and remaining checks
Conflicting sources [Conflict]
Current GRE exemption supersedes old required/benchmark language. Current English policy supersedes old
paper-TOEFL thresholds. Departmental late consideration versus central form closure, midnight wording, and
tuition/stipend versus conditional summer descriptions need clarification. [s1] [s3] [s4] [s5] [s6]
Checks still needed [Unresolved]
Confirm 2027 dates and midnight clock; endorsement interview sequence; pending-degree English waiver;
reference-send trigger and replacement; all live writing limits; optional GRE treatment; exact paid months,
summer, fee/health coverage and support years; commitment deadline.
